about: The Act shelf (STATUTE_COVERAGE_PLAN.md step 2): Acts whose full text is loaded from India Code by build_act_chunks.py, checked against India Code's own PDF. 'corrections' are exact replacements of slips in India Code's database, each shown to be what the PDF reads; 'accepted' are spelling variants that are not slips. Nothing here says the text has been read by a person.

pointers.why: Section 8 makes GIVING an undue advantage to a public servant an offence; its provisos exempt a person who was compelled to give it only if he reports the matter to the law enforcement authority or investigating agency within seven days of giving it. A question in which the person paid or was made to pay never uses the words 'section 8', and a search by meaning ranks the offence of TAKING (s.7) first (staging 2026-10-17: the tehsildar answer said nothing about the payer's own position).

corrections.from: upon whom talaq is pronounced or any person related to her by blood or marriage; is pronounced with the permission of the Magistrate
corrections.to: upon whom talaq is pronounced with the permission of the Magistrate
corrections.why: India Code's database has copied the end of clause (a) into clause (b): 'or any person related to her by blood or marriage; is pronounced'. The PDF's clause (b) (printed page 3, read on the rendered page as well as in its text layer) says compounding is 'at the instance of the married Muslim woman upon whom talaq is pronounced with the permission of the Magistrate': at the woman's instance only. As the database has it, a reader would think a relative may compound the offence. The PDF prints no comma after 'pronounced' and none is added.
